name: Taking Back Sunday
label: Victory
lede: Taking Back Sunday cut its debut in two weeks for $10,000 and watched it go platinum 21 years later. In between, two members quit, Warner Bros. took the band to No. 2, and the Tell All Your Friends line-up played together again in 2010.

eras.title: A bassist leaves, a kid from North Carolina sings
eras.text: Eddie Reyes and Jesse Lacey started the band in Amityville. Lacey lasted a few months, left after a clash with John Nolan and formed Brand New; a North Carolina kid took the bass, then the microphone, and by December 2001 the band had a deal with Victory.

years.h: Eddie Reyes and Jesse Lacey start a band in Amityville
years.p: John Nolan plays lead guitar, Antonio Longo sings and Steven DeJoseph drums. The name comes from a song by Long Island band The Waiting Process.

years.src: Wikipedia: Taking Back Sunday · Wikipedia: Tell All Your Friends
yt: Brand New and Taking Back Sunday live, Jan 5, 2002
years.h: Lacey quits after a clash with Nolan and starts [[Brand New|9311e2bc-bb3f-44cf-90d8-b1fe6912b60b]]
years.p: Lacey had lasted three or four months. Per Wikipedia it was a personal incident with Nolan, and the feud spilled onto records, including Brand New's Seventy Times 7.
years.xp:
Alternative Press, as Wikipedia quotes it, called the split "one of the most public intra-band rivalries in emo history." Seventy Times 7 appeared on Brand New's 2001 debut Your Favorite Weapon.

Taking Back Sunday answered on Tell All Your Friends. Wikipedia says There's No 'I' in Team is about the falling-out, which it describes as starting when Nolan romanced Lacey's girlfriend at a party.

Nolan and Lacey eventually reconciled, though Adam Lazzara was still speaking about Lacey unfavorably in 2015.

years.h: Adam Lazzara moves from bass to the microphone
years.p: Lazzara had moved up from North Carolina after meeting the band at a show, and joined on bass. Mark O'Connell replaces drummer Steven DeJoseph and Shaun Cooper takes the bass.

years.h: A demo passed along by a friend gets the band onto Victory
years.p: The friend handed it to Victory A&R rep Angel Juarbe. The band was in the studio the same month.

eras.title: A debut that kept charting for 68 weeks
eras.text: Tell All Your Friends sold 2,000 copies in its first week and then stayed on Billboard's Heatseekers chart for more than a year. Meanwhile the line-up that made it came apart, and the band had to be rebuilt on the road.

yt: Cute Without the 'E' (Cut from the Team), official video
years.h: Tell All Your Friends costs $10,000 and goes platinum 21 years on
years.p: Cut in two weeks at Big Blue Meenie in Jersey City with Sal Villanueva, it sold 2,000 copies in week one, went gold in 2005 and platinum in June 2023.
years.xp:
The band showed up without a drum kit, assuming the studio had one. Engineer Tim Gilles told them no major studio in America owns its own, and added, as Wikipedia prints it, "You've gotta be fucking kidding me." They commuted in from Long Island around day jobs; Shaun Cooper recorded all his bass in four hours.

At the mix, the band found the studio had sped the piano intro of The Blue Channel up to match the rest of the song, four times faster. They were told they were out of time and budget. The number on the cover, 152, is Exit 152 off Interstate 40 in Mebane, North Carolina, where Lazzara and friends stopped at a gas station.

Victory handed out 20,000 sampler discs in Chicago, New York and Los Angeles, at about $100,000. The album became the label's longest-running release: 68 weeks on Heatseekers, 78 on Independent Albums.

Touring cost something too. Four shows into the Best Revenge Tour in September 2002, Lazzara fell off the stage, gashed his face in two places, dislocated his hip and left the tour.
play: Cute Without the 'E' (Cut from the Team)

years.h: Christian Winters shoots the first video, three weeks before the album
years.p: Great Romances of the 20th Century is released March 4 and goes to radio March 12.
years.xp:
Winters, a friend of the band, directed the next two videos as well. For Cute Without the 'E' (Cut from the Team), which premiered December 10 on Launch.com, Lazzara first pitched men fighting women; Winters and Victory said no, and it became a riff on Fight Club.

The Great Romances video samples audio from the 1996 film Beautiful Girls.

years.cap: Opening for Piebald, with John Nolan and Shaun Cooper still in the line-up
years.src: Wikipedia: Taking Back Sunday · Wikipedia: Straylight Run
yt: The first-album line-up live, Boulder, Aug 9, 2002
years.h: Nolan and Cooper walk out after Skate & Surf
years.p: Per Wikipedia, Lazzara was drinking heavily and had cheated on Nolan's sister Michelle. Nolan found his apology at Skate & Surf insincere; two days later he and Cooper were gone.
years.xp:
The official reason was exhaustion from touring. Wikipedia says the truth also involved constant fighting and disputes over songwriting credit.

Nolan and Cooper formed [[Straylight Run|ffe16bba-4d84-409b-8f22-5242c60b930f]] in Baldwin, New York with Michelle DaRosa (Nolan's sister) and Will Noon. Their 2004 debut, also on Victory, sold over 11,000 copies in its first week.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tell All Your Friends · Wikipedia: Where You Want to Be
years.h: Fred Mascherino and Matt Rubano, both jazz-trained, take the empty chairs
years.p: Mascherino comes from [[Breaking Pangaea|b2f5dbf0-572f-419e-a3c0-7d0cae9c609c]] on guitar and vocals, Rubano plays bass. Lazzara said they cleaned up and tightened the band's sound.
years.xp:
Mascherino joined on August 5, 2003. Rubano came in at O'Connell's request, and according to Wikipedia he wasn't a fan of emo before he joined.

The new hires went straight into a video. For You're So Last Summer, shot in November 2003 at Fulton Park in Brooklyn, the band cast Public Enemy's Flavor Flav. Lazzara explained: "the funniest way to do that was to use Flavor Flav." With two members gone, he said, they needed a way to bring in the new ones without Mascherino singing the old part.

eras.title: The jump to a major
eras.text: Where You Want to Be debuted at No. 3, still Victory's highest chart peak, and the label's founder picked a fight with the RIAA over the gold plaque. Then the band signed to Warner Bros., and Louder Now landed one place higher.

years.src: Wikipedia: Where You Want to Be
years.h: Where You Want to Be opens at No. 3 on 163,000 copies
years.p: Self-financed and cut with Lou Giordano in Brooklyn and Hoboken, it sold 634,000 by June 2005. That's still Victory's highest chart peak.
years.xp:
It spent 50 weeks at the top of Billboard's Independent Albums chart and was the best-selling independent rock album within a year of release. Rolling Stone named it one of the top fifty records of 2004.

The This Photograph Is Proof (I Know You Know) video was directed by [[Blink-182|0743b15a-3c32-48c8-ad58-cb325350befa]]'s Tom DeLonge and shot across Dallas, Los Angeles and Nashville in 48 hours. The A Decade Under the Influence video put remote-control monster trucks on warehouse tracks.

Critics split: Metacritic lands at 74, and USA Today called it "more winsome than generic" while admitting the "cobbled together emo clichés."

years.big: "From where I sit, this is another attempt by the RIAA and its major-label partners to victimize, abuse and belittle an independent record company."
years.src: Wikipedia: Where You Want to Be
years.h: Gold for Where You Want to Be, and Victory's founder objects
years.p: Tony Brummel, on the first gold record of any Victory artist, certified in July 2005 at 500,000 copies. The band's manager Jillian Newman answered him.
years.xp: Newman, who had managed the band since June 2002, was blunt: "I don't understand how a label gets victimized by receiving a sales award."

years.cap: On stage, August 25, 2005, two months after the Warner Bros. deal
years.h: Warner Bros. gets the band, and Victory keeps the catalog
years.p: The June 10 deal ends the band's run at Victory after two albums. Victory goes on releasing compilations of the songs.

years.h: Louder Now makes it to No. 2 on the Billboard 200
years.p: Recorded at Barefoot Studios in Los Angeles with Eric Valentine, who made [[Queens of the Stone Age|7dc8f5bd-9d0b-4087-9f73-dc164950bbd8]]' Songs for the Deaf. It sold over 900,000 copies.

years.h: Victory's Notes from the Past arrives 16 months after the band left
years.p: A compilation of four Tell All Your Friends songs, six from Where You Want to Be and two B-sides.

years.big: "There were just problems between the five of us about writing."
years.h: Fred Mascherino heads off to The Color Fred
years.p: Mascherino on why he left, in October 2007. Matthew Fazzi takes his place.
years.xp: Mascherino went on to focus on his solo project, The Color Fred. Guitarist and backing vocalist Fazzi replaced him for New Again.

eras.title: The originals come home
eras.text: After one album with Matthew Fazzi, the band admitted it wasn't having fun. John Nolan and Shaun Cooper, whose Straylight Run had just gone on hiatus, came back, and the Tell All Your Friends line-up was whole again.

years.h: New Again: the one record with Matthew Fazzi
years.p: Taking Back Sunday's fourth album was previewed by Sink into Me on Zane Lowe's BBC Radio 1 show in April.
years.xp: It includes Carpathia, which per the band has the first bass solos in any Taking Back Sunday song.

years.cap: The reunited line-up live, with John Nolan and Shaun Cooper back
years.src: Wikipedia: Taking Back Sunday · Wikipedia: Straylight Run · Wikipedia: Tell All Your Friends
years.h: Nolan and Cooper come back, seven years after they left
years.p: Matt Rubano and Matthew Fazzi left on March 29. The band said it had been miserable without the originals, and meeting in Texas, the chemistry was still there.
years.xp:
Straylight Run had announced an indefinite hiatus in February 2010, citing financial reasons; Nolan's and Cooper's return was confirmed March 31.

Per Wikipedia, the meeting in 2003 where Nolan raised leaving was his last contact with Lazzara for seven years.

years.h: The self-titled album reunites the band with Eric Valentine
years.p: The reunited five's first record, led by Faith (When I Let You Down) in May.

eras.title: Playing the old records back
eras.text: Taking Back Sunday played its debut start to finish for the tenth anniversary, lost a founder to alcoholism, and for the twentieth let a coin pick the second album each night.

years.cap: Playing for US troops at Camp Arifjan, Kuwait
years.h: Ten years on, Tell All Your Friends gets played start to finish
years.p: Bayside is main support. The same summer, Taking Back Sunday plays every date of the 2012 Warped Tour.
years.xp: The vinyl reissue reached No. 8 on Billboard's Vinyl Albums chart in November 2012. An acoustic version recorded in Los Angeles and Chicago followed in June 2013, then a double DVD with TAYF10: Live from Starland Ballroom in December.

years.h: Spencer Chamberlain of Underoath fills in for Lazzara
years.p: Lazzara's son was born prematurely, and [[Underoath|674a7e8c-9682-419a-8e05-2358e28b5359]]'s Chamberlain sings nine shows, October 25 to November 2.

years.h: Happiness Is lands on Hopeless Records
years.p: The sixth album includes violinist Dylan Ebrahimian, who played with the band at an acoustic show at Stony Brook University in November 2013.

years.h: Two years on, Tidal Wave
years.p: The seventh album, written in the gaps between tours for Happiness Is.

years.h: Eddie Reyes steps away, saying alcoholism is why
years.p: The last founding member besides John Nolan leaves in April 2018, saying he hopes to come back one day.

years.h: A specially made coin decides the second album each night
years.p: On the 20th-anniversary tour's two-night stands, it picks Louder Now or Where You Want to Be for the night. Tell All Your Friends gets played every night, and the Twenty compilation comes out the same day.

eras.title: 152, and the drummer who left
eras.text: The band made 152 for Fantasy and played Coachella. Then its drummer of 23 years left, and later sued.

years.h: Cappadonna of the Wu-Tang Clan joins Verrazzano Villains
years.p: A collaboration with Q-Unique, DJ Eclipse and [[Wu-Tang Clan|0febdcf7-4e1f-4661-9493-b40427de2c13]]'s Cappadonna. In June, Taking Back Sunday plays shows with [[Thursday|0acae232-d31a-4211-b6d0-6af1b6350274]] and [[Piebald|403bc4cd-602c-4b59-8379-05cb24f66aa6]].

years.cap: Taking Back Sunday at Riot Fest
years.h: 152 arrives on Fantasy Records
years.p: The eighth album follows the single The One, the band's first original music in four years. They play Coachella in April 2024.
years.xp: The title shares its number with the cover of Tell All Your Friends, which shows Exit 152 off Interstate 40 in Mebane, North Carolina.

years.h: Fred Mascherino plays with the band again at Starland Ballroom
years.p: His first time on stage with Taking Back Sunday since 2007, in Sayreville, New Jersey, for Liar (It Takes One to Know One) and MakeDamnSure.

years.h: Drummer Mark O'Connell announces he's out after 23 years
years.p: Eddie Reyes had already said so on a podcast in December. O'Connell cited creative differences and a lack of support while he committed to sobriety.

years.h: O'Connell sues his former bandmates
years.p: The suit is for defamation and alleges false claims and withheld royalty payments.

years.cap: Live at Gallagher Square, Houston, September 28, 2025
years.h: Nolan takes a break from the road, and Mascherino steps back in
years.p: Nolan steps off tour to spend time with family; Mascherino rejoins in a touring role. The plan is festival dates as a six-piece with Lazzara, Nolan and Mascherino sharing vocals.
